bull_bear.body: No major M&A; focus on organic reinvestment in store upgrades and marketing; Dividend of INR 2 per share declared for FY26; Working capital days structurally higher (debtor days ~140-146) due to risk-absorption model for franchisees, but no material bad debts.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical tensions (West Asia) impacting consumer sentiment and input costs; Inflationary pressure on discretionary spending; Execution risk in transitioning store network without disrupting cash flows; Sustained high ad spend failing to convert to volume growth.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic on long-term brand equity but realistic/prudent on near-term numbers; Emphasizes 'transition year' narrative, prioritizing sustainability over speed; Transparent about margin trade-offs for brand building.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management explicitly states they are not raising prices despite premiumization, relying on 'elevated environment' to drive value; The 'risk absorption model' leads to structurally higher debtor days compared to peers but claims zero historical write-offs; Online channel is viewed as a discovery tool for offline sales rather than a primary profit center currently.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Debt-free balance sheet as at Mar-26: non-current borrowings Rs 0.0 Cr and current borrowings Rs 0.0 Cr (vs Rs 1.1 Cr and Rs 0.3 Cr at Mar-25), with total equity of Rs 438.6 Cr and cash and cash equivalents of Rs 52.4 Cr plus Rs 20.2 Cr of other bank balances.
- Working capital is consciously heavy: net working capital days of 184 (FY25), 196 (FY26) and 176* (Jun-26), driven by debtor days of 133 / 147 / 118 and inventory days of 67 / 65 / 74 against creditor days of only 16 / 16 / 17.
- Cash flow from operations (post IND AS 116) of Rs 159 Cr in FY25, Rs 132 Cr in FY26 and Rs 33 Cr in Jun-26; historical net cash from financing activities was an outflow in every year FY22-FY26 (Rs -89.7 Cr in FY26).
- Trailing-twelve-month return ratios as of Jun 30, 2026: RoCE 12.9% and RoE 10.1%, against FY26 RoE 8.0% (deck's RoCE = EBIT / Average Capital Employed, RoE = PAT / Average Equity).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Nearly three-decade-old brand ('MUFTI') recognised as an Indian Power Brand, closely synonymous with the Company itself
- Asset-light model with no manufacturing fixed costs, providing flexibility without losing consistency
- Curated product philosophy and strong design control positioned to bridge international premium brands and Indian counterparts
- Pan-India multichannel distribution network of 429 EBOs, 148 LFS and 1,336 MBOs across 583 cities, supported by a growing digital ecosystem
- Muftisphere loyalty ecosystem with a database of over 3 million customers; own-website revenue grew approximately 74% year-on-year in FY26
- Balance sheet entirely free of financial debt, with brand-transformation investments funded wholly from internal accruals
- No material write-off from trade receivables across the Company's history, reflecting the quality of franchise and trade-partner relationships
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Demand sensitivity to discretionary consumer spending — The branded apparel industry navigated a challenging FY26 marked by subdued consumer sentiment and weaker discretionary spending, particularly in Tier II and Tier III markets; Q3 FY26 was muted with the festive season falling short of expectations and lower footfall across retail touchpoints, weighing on industry-wide revenue growth.
- Supply chain concentration and disruption — A supply chain disruption in Bangladesh delayed product availability during the year, along with logistics delays and raw material cost pressures affecting timely availability and quarterly revenue; raw material cost pressures and sourcing diversification risk are flagged as continuing key monitoring areas.
- Intensifying competition from well-funded D2C and international brands — Domestic brands, international entrants and digitally native fashion platforms target the same consumer base; several private-equity-backed D2C-native brands deploy disproportionately large marketing budgets relative to revenue, intensifying brand-visibility competition for established offline-first players, while fast fashion/value retailers pressure lower price segments and global premium brands strengthen their India presence in the aspirational category.
- Digital/D2C relevance risk requiring sustained investment — The growing consumer preference for digitally native D2C brands creates relevance risk among younger consumers; while the Company's own D2C business has grown strongly, the channel requires sustained investment in technology, marketing and consumer experience to remain competitive.
- Retail network productivity — Underperforming stores were flagged as affecting overall network productivity and operational efficiency, requiring ongoing rationalisation (closure of underperforming stores) alongside selective premium-format additions.
- Regulatory / GST-driven margin pressure — GST reforms during the year created temporary pressure on margins; the Company passed on tax benefits on products priced below Rs 2,500 to consumers while absorbing additional costs on premium products to support consumer traction, rather than raising prices.
- Cyber and information security risk — The Risk Management Committee periodically reviews cyber risk and cyber security exposures, including threats from malware, viruses and web application attacks, relevant given the Company's growing digital and e-commerce operations.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Offline Retail: ~91% of revenue, SSSG flattish in Q4; Online: ~9% of revenue (5% own website, rest marketplaces), grew 75% YoY in FY26 but lower EBITDA due to discounts; Loyalty (Muftisphere): 2.5mn members, 35-40% contribution to EBO revenue, avg ticket INR 5,200.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- "Creative, Bold and Expressive Clothing for the Contemporary Indian Man" - a casual-led, denim-led brand deliberately placed in the mid-premium to premium price range, with expressiveness and boldness in design cited as the differentiator from competition.
- Reinvented brand identity described as "A new identity rooted in 28 years of authenticity - ready for India's premium evolution", with MUFTI 2.0 intended "to rekindle demand and unlock the next phase of growth".
- Multi-channel pan-India distribution: 1,913 touchpoints, 427 EBOs across 231 towns & cities, presence in 583 cities in India as of Jun 30, 2026, and a customer database of over 2.5 million on "Muftisphere".
- "Scalable and Asset Light Business Model" - the company comprehensively focuses on design and outsources manufacturing, working with 50+ fabric and accessories suppliers and 50+ manufacturing partners.
- The deck argues its optically weak working-capital metrics are a strategic choice, not weakness: Credo retains inventory and markdown risk that most retail models push to store operators, using "our balance sheet strength to absorb partner risk, lock in favourable pricing, and ensure product freshness".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Demand environment] Management flags "continued softness in discretionary spending" and a global environment where "geopolitical tensions likely to keep consumers cautious and near-term demand visibility uneven", while pointing to India's growing aspirations and the evolving casual lifestyle segment as the long-term opportunity.
- [Margin trade-off] The deck explicitly attributes the Q1 FY27 EBITDA decline to brand investment - marketing spend of Rs 10.7 crore (8.5% of total revenue) versus Rs 5.4 crore in Q1 FY26 - framing it as an investment in long-term salience rather than an operational miss.
- [Promoter-led] Mr. Kamal Khushlani is Promoter and Chairman & MD and authors the deck's outlook commentary; CFO is Mr. Rasik Mittal; investor relations is outsourced to Strategic Growth Advisors (SGA).
- [Reporting basis change] Historical P&L, balance sheet and cash flow columns for FY22-FY25 are footnoted "*On Consolidated Basis" while FY26 / Mar-26 carries no such marker, so the five-year series is not stated on a single reporting basis.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Advance the MUFTI 2.0 transformation, anchored on three pillars: Reinventing the Store, Redefining the Brand Experience, and Reigniting the Spark
- Premiumise store experience and merchandise architecture; open new-identity stores in premium malls/high streets while exiting underperforming outlets, prioritising network quality over store count
- Scale advertising and branding investment (digital campaigns, influencer collaborations, content) to build brand salience and long-term demand
- Accelerate the digital/D2C channel (own website, omnichannel presence) as both a sales engine and a storytelling platform, deepening engagement with digitally native consumers
- Maintain financial discipline: fund brand transformation and store expansion wholly from internal accruals and stay debt-free
- Deepen use of data and technology, including AI, for sharper micro-merchandising, design, content and marketing
- The Board's stated dividend approach endeavours for fairness, consistency and sustainability while distributing profits to Members (per the Company's Dividend Distribution Policy referenced in governance disclosures). For FY26, the AGM notice tables a resolution to declare a dividend of Rs 2.00 per equity share, to be paid out of the profits of the Company, subject to shareholder approval. No further capital-allocation philosophy (debt policy, reinvestment intent) is disclosed within this routed bundle.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: FY26 was described as a watershed year with the full-scale launch of the MUFTI 2.0 transformation: a reimagined store identity with refreshed retail design language, elevated merchandise architecture, intensified brand-building investment across digital and traditional media, and deeper engagement through the Muftisphere loyalty platform. During FY26 the Company launched 28 stores under the new MUFTI 2.0 retail identity (14 new stores and 14 renovated stores), including its first flagship MUFTI 2.0 Premium Identity Store at Phoenix Mall, Mumbai, alongside other premium corridors (Sky City Mall Borivali, Acropolis Mall, Lulu Mall Bengaluru and Kochi, Inorbit Mall Hubli). Across the wider network, the Company opened 34 stores and closed 46 underperforming stores during the year as part of a deliberate quality-over-scale strategy, ending FY26 with 429 EBOs (233 cities), 1,336 MBOs and 148 LFS, and 1,913+ total retail touchpoints. Expansion continues to be funded through internal accruals while the Company remains debt-free. For FY27, the Company plans to close approximately 20 stores and open 20 new stores with continued emphasis on premium locations, and intends to strategically add nearly 20 premium stores under the MUFTI 2.0 format to further elevate brand perception.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Long-term Indian menswear market opportunity (USD 21.9 billion in 2025, projected to reach USD 42.4 billion by 2034) remains intact even though the mid-premium and premium segments face near-term headwinds from cautious discretionary spending
- Structural demand drivers cited: rising disposable incomes, urbanisation, growing fashion awareness among younger/Gen Z consumers, shift from unbranded to branded apparel, and e-commerce/D2C expansion reaching deeper into Tier II/III cities
- Policy tailwinds - income tax relief for individuals earning up to Rs 12 lakh and GST rationalisation - expected to release purchasing power into the Indian middle class and support consumer sentiment, though full effect had yet to materialise
- Near-term demand headwinds through FY26: cautious consumer sentiment in discretionary fashion, lower footfalls, a festive quarter that fell short of expectations industry-wide, and a temporary sourcing disruption from Bangladesh that delayed product availability in H1 FY26
- Margin narrative: FY26 EBITDA margin (26.0%) declined versus prior year, reflecting a deliberate increase in advertising, branding and premium-location costs as an investment in the brand's future rather than a structural cost pressure; gross margin held stable at 58.4%
- GST reform in Q3 FY26 changed the tax rate on garments below Rs 2,500; the Company chose to pass the savings on to consumers rather than retain them, to protect consumer trust and sales volumes
- Looking ahead, geopolitical uncertainty is flagged as a source of rising inflation and input costs that adds complexity to planning, though supplier relationships built over years are cited as a mitigant
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Credo Brands is executing a strategic 'Mufti 2.0' transformation, prioritizing long-term brand equity via premium store formats and doubled advertising spend (8-10% of revenue) over near-term growth, resulting in flat revenue and compressed FY27 margin guidance despite improved product mix. The company is consciously trading immediate profitability for market relevance, expecting mid-single-digit growth in FY27 as it rationalizes its store network (closing ~20 underperformers, opening ~20 premium units).

open.item: The Board has recommended a final dividend of Rs 2.00 (100%) per Equity Share of Rs 2.00 each for FY26, involving a cash outflow of Rs 130.74 million, subject to Members' approval.

In FY27 the Company will continue opening stores under the new MUFTI identity in premium locations, scale advertising and branding investment further, and deepen the consumer's relationship with the brand.

In FY27, the Company plans to close approximately 20 stores and open 20 new stores with continued emphasis on premium locations, and intends to strategically add nearly 20 premium stores under the MUFTI 2.0 format to further elevate brand perception.

Management expects the long-term benefits of its premiumisation initiatives (MUFTI 2.0) to begin emerging over the next two to three years as brand-building spends stabilise and the new store network reaches maturity.

The Company remains focused on improving retail network productivity by closing underperforming stores and selectively opening experience-led stores in better locations, to build a healthier, more productive and more aspirational retail network over time.

The Board has recommended the re-appointment of Mr. Kamal Khushlani as Chairman and Managing Director for a further period of five years with effect from March 8, 2027 (on expiry of his present term), subject to Shareholders' approval at the ensuing AGM.

The Company remains focused on improving productivity across the retail network by closing underperforming stores and selectively opening experience-led stores in better locations, aiming for a healthier, more productive and more aspirational network over time.
